subject: Patch acceptance timeline, fallback plan, and CVE observability links
messages:

Cc: FinWell Security Ops <sec-ops@finwell.com>

Subject: Request: SLA for critical patching + evidence links

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As part of our SOC 2 evidence collection we need a short statement of Redwood's SLA and operational plan for high-severity CVEs (CRITICAL / CVSS >= 9.0). Specifically:

- Expected time-to-patch for infra-exploitable CVEs that affect customer endpoints
- Canary/fallback procedure if a patch causes regressions
- Where we can pull audit-ready evidence for the scan cadence and remediation status (exportable CSV or Drive link)

Can you share the acceptance timeline and any runbook links? FinWell's internal control owners need this by EOD Monday to include in the audit pack.

Appreciate it —
Alice Park
Security Compliance Lead | FinWell Financial
alice.park@finwell.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA for critical patching + evidence links

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: for CRITICAL infra-exploitable CVEs we target an operational SLA of 72 hours for mitigation and verified rollout on Hosted/Dedicated customers; for Private deployments we provide the remediation playbook and recommended patch window and will support emergency backporting per contract.

Attached is our internal patch acceptance and fallback playbook (redwood_patch_plan_v1.2.pdf) and a brief canary/fallback checklist (fallback_canary_playbook.md). Highlights: 

- T0 identification: automated alert + triage within 4 hours.
- T0–T24: triage, patch verification on internal dogfood + replication on a single canary cluster.
- T24–T48: staged rollout to 10–30% of capacity (regionally aware), health checks every 10m.
- T48–T72: full rollout if canary is green; otherwise rollback and apply hotfix.

Canary/fallback specifics: we use a two-tier canary (canary-1 for synthetic and sampling traffic; canary-2 mirrors 2% live production traffic). If error rate increases >150% or P95 latency regresses >30%, automatic rollback to previous model/binary is triggered and paging occurs.

For audit evidence: we expose a CSV export of CVE remediation status (cve_tracking_export_20270110.csv) and a read-only Drive folder with historical scan artifacts. The drive link is in the related_links field below and the observability dashboard provides token-level traces for the rollout windows.

Next steps I propose:
1) We share the Drive link and CSV export with your control owners (done).
2) Laura to confirm SOC 2 wording for the acceptance timeline (can you approve the 72-hour commitment?)
3) If you want a signed attestation, we can generate a short DocuSign agreement covering the SLA and emergency support terms.

Let me know if you want a 15-min sync early next week to walk the control owners through the canary thresholds.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director of Sales, Security & Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
(650) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_patch_plan_v1.2.pdf, fallback_canary_playbook.md

Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2027 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA for critical patching + evidence links

Alice—and team—

I'm good to confirm the 72-hour operational target for remediation and verified rollout on Hosted/Dedicated customers as described. A couple of caveats to be explicit about for SOC 2: 

- Our 72-hour commitment is measured from our triage (T0) as described in Karthik's note (automated detection + human triage).
- For Private/on-prem customers, we offer the same playbook but remediation time depends on customer's maintenance windows and access; we include emergency backporting support under our enterprise contract.

As requested, I've exported a snapshot of our CVE tracking for the last 90 days and attached cve_tracking_export_20270110.csv. That contains vulnerabilities, assigned owners, status, and timestamps for discovery->patch->verify. You can include that as evidence in the audit packet.

Operational controls we rely on for the SLA: automated scanning every 24 hours, prioritized triage based on exploitability signals, runbooked canary rollout with automatic health-based rollback. We also keep an immutable audit log for every rollout (Drive + observability link).

If FinWell's auditors need a short signed attestation (one paragraph) confirming the 72-hour target, we can prepare and route via DocuSign (I recommend adding the DocuSign link to the audit packet).

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
VP, Trust & Security | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: cve_tracking_export_20270110.csv

Laura / Karthik —

Thanks, this is exactly what we needed. We will include the CSV and Drive link in the SOC 2 evidence folder. Two quick asks before we close: 

1) Please send the one-paragraph signed attestation via DocuSign (DOCUSIGN:ds12345-ff-2027) so our control owner can attach it to the control narrative.
2) Can you confirm the retention window for the CVE audit logs (how long the immutable rollout log is retained)? Our policy requires 2 years.

If you can reply with those two items today we'll mark the control as "evidence submitted".

—Alice
